summary: Built in 1937 and used by the Aircraft Warning Service in WWII, the Pinyon Peak lookout was destroyed in the 1977 Marble Cone Fire; a trip report disputes the bare site.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301, open steel tower on a K-brace
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the 1977 Marble Cone Fire. The register says nothing remains; a trip report describes four concrete pillars on the east summit.
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Los Padres National Forest

events.note: Constructed 1937 (register). The Los Padres lookout history also gives 1937, with a 36-foot tower built by the CCC.
Destroyed in the Marble Cone Fire (register and Los Padres history). The fire burned in August 1977 in Monterey County.
Date registered December 22, 2019 as US 1870, CA 65

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register describes a 30-foot K-brace open steel tower; the Los Padres lookout history gives 36 feet with a 14-by-14 cab. The story gives no height. Not resolved.

The register says nothing remains at the site. A trip report describes four concrete pillars on the east summit and calls them the only remains of a lookout. The trip report's date is not in the text read. Both accounts are reported in the story; not resolved.

sources.title: Trip report on Bear Mountain and Pinyon Peak

notes_for_editor: Height disagrees: 30 feet (register) against 36 feet (Los Padres history via Forest Lookouts). The trip report is undated in the text we read; find its date before publishing the remains line with more weight. The register's 'Nothing remains at the site' conflicts with the trip report's four pillars. The Marble Cone Fire facts come from Wikipedia; its cited sources were not read. The Santa Maria Daily Times quote is secondhand through the Forest Lookouts page. Access rules today are not in any source read. Sid Ormsbee lookout is a different site; it is mentioned only as a warning.
